article.name: Engram Alpha
article.summary: Engram Alpha is a local-first graph memory for software projects, exposed through an MCP and HTTP core, CLI, IDE extensions, and a web pane. It stores typed nodes and relations in one graph file per project, then serves hybrid keyword/vector retrieval with graph context, trust and confidence signals. This review is source-based; no runtime or benchmark was executed.

who_what.text: The official README describes Engram Alpha as a local graph memory shared by coding assistants, with a Rust core, Vue/TypeScript pane and IDE integrations. This review does not infer an individual maintainer identity.

architecture.text: The Rust workspace separates core, MCP, HTTP, CLI and evaluation crates. The graph schema holds typed nodes and edges, a suspects queue, metadata, tasks, and an append-only mutation journal. Node fields include source/session, created and validity times, tags, code refs, custom fields and trust timestamps.

The README and storage guide describe TepinDB as the graph-file backend, SQLite as a migration source, and local embedding, reranking and NLI components as configurable. These are project architecture statements, not measured resource results.

behavior.text: The checked write path embeds a proposed note, checks same-type current near-duplicates, and either returns a match for caller-side merging or creates a node and returns warnings/suspect pairs. Node operations validate configured types and fields and journal updates.

Replacement archives the old node behind a replaces relation; explicit deletion can mint a Tombstone with removed content and reason, while a direct delete path removes the node and connected edges. Merge rehomes relationships. Secure erasure from backups or storage media was not established.

Search fuses keyword and vector retrieval, optionally reranks a bounded candidate set, applies delivery filters and session diversity, adds one-hop neighbors, attaches standing information, and stamps returned hits for observability. Confidence is calibrated only when the reranker is available; runtime quality was not measured.

Project roots map to separate graph files. Bound sessions use their selected project; the home graph can accompany briefs, and all-project search/claim checks are read-only and mark foreign hits with project provenance. No OS-level local-user access boundary was established by this source review.

Node source and session fields plus audit action, before/after snapshots, front-end origin, session, working directory, process and version provide provenance. They support traceability, not proof that a memory is correct or that downstream claims cite it faithfully.

Source-inspected efficiency features include FTS indexes, vectors, bounded reranker candidate fetch, result limits and one-hop neighbor caps. Returned-hit last_seen is observability-only by source comments. No latency, cost, token, storage or operational-load measurements were collected.

metrics.evidence: Confidence verdicts and project negative-question evaluation are documented; this review ran no answerability or abstention workload.
Supersession, conflict review, trust/decay, and temporal fields are source-inspected; correction accuracy and stale-value rate were not measured.
Direct deletion and Tombstone paths were inspected; no residual-read or secure-erasure probe was run.
Project-specific routing and optional cross-project reads were inspected; no isolation workload was run.
Source/session lineage, audit context, graph relations and standing were inspected; answer support precision and citation coverage were not scored.
No token, provider billing, or storage measurements were collected.

limits.text: This is a source review at the verified main head. Engram Alpha, tests and benchmarks were not run.

Live retrieval quality, actual abstention behavior, secure erasure, access control against other local processes, model quality, scaling, latency, and cost remain unknown from this review. The GitHub REST API was rate-limited; official Git remote and shallow checkout agreed on branch and full head SHA.

benchmark.note: No Engram Alpha runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run. Project metric definitions and comparison fixtures are not Engram results.
